name: Cancer of Unknown Primary Site

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic criteria for Cancer of Unknown Primary

criteria.description: Histopathological confirmation of metastatic malignancy without identifiable primary tumor after comprehensive evaluation
Negative findings for primary tumor on extensive imaging including CT, MRI, and PET scans
Immunohistochemical profile inconsistent or non-diagnostic for known primary tumor origin
Exclusion of primary tumor by clinical examination and endoscopic evaluations

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of metastatic cancer with no identifiable primary tumor after comprehensive imaging and immunohistochemical evaluation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires multidisciplinary approach including pathology, radiology, and clinical oncology.

searchTerms: lymph node swelling without known cause

laboratory: Elevated tumor markers may be nonspecific
Anemia and other cytopenias in marrow involvement
imaging: Multiple metastatic lesions on CT, MRI, or PET scans
Absence of identifiable primary tumor on comprehensive imaging
genetic: No specific genetic mutation universally identified

other: Immunohistochemistry panels used to narrow down possible primary sites

distinguishingFeatures: Identifiable primary tumor on imaging or biopsy
Immunohistochemical profile consistent with known primary
Lymph node biopsy showing lymphoid malignancy
Different immunophenotypic markers compared to carcinoma

redFlags: Severe hypercalcemia or other paraneoplastic syndromes
